St James Senior Boys’ School
Founded in 1975, we are an independent day school for boys aged 11-18 located in Ashford, Surrey.
The St James Difference
Sara | Current Parent
“The best things for us as parents, is seeing what a lovely, confident, young man our son is turning into, he is really thriving at St James, and we are so happy with the school.”
Rowan | Head Boy
“St James has been instrumental in the development of my character. I’ve learned so many lessons, both the easy and hard way, and been able to realise and overcome various challenges. “
Agastya | Year 9 Pupil
“I have made a lot of friends here in St James and the best thing about them is that when I need something, they’ll always help me. Everyone has friends here.”
Meet our Head
“Our distinctive education unites a philosophical approach to the development of essential life skills”
Admissions
“We are delighted that you are considering St James as an educational pathway for your child.”
Meditation
In keeping with the Ethos of St James Schools, pupils practise regular pauses or times of quiet throughout the day to promote their appreciation and understanding of mindfulness.
Philosophy
St James cares for a pupil’s spirit, mind and body. All pupils study Philosophy to explore and challenge ideas in a respectful and inclusive way.
Vegetarianism
Creating a vegetarian school in 1975 was a reflection of the belief that humans should be kind to themselves, others, and environment to grow holistically.

pageCache.pageTitle: Jesus Christ Superstar! - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Jesus Christ Superstar!
Students took to the stage to showcase their acting, singing and dancing in an exciting production of Jesus Christ Superstar!
On Wednesday 3 December and Thursday 4 December, in collaboration with St James Senior Girls’ School, students delivered two memorable performances that powerfully told the story of Jesus’ final week of life, while capturing the spirit of Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice’s legendary rock opera.
Reflecting on the production, Head of Drama Andy Camichel commented:
“Our students have shown remarkable creativity, energy and commitment in bringing this powerful story to life. From the first rehearsal to the performance, they have worked tirelessly, and we couldn’t be prouder of what they have achieved.”
Following the performance, Head of English Mrs Reid wrote:
“Of course, the main highlight was the exceptional quality of the student performances. The whole cast and crew did a phenomenal job and staff, students and families alike could not be prouder.”
Mrs Lodder, a parent at St James Senior Boys’ School, also shared her praise:
“The energy in the room was infectious, and it was evident how much fun the boys were having on stage. We feel incredibly grateful that St James offers such amazing opportunities to explore passions beyond the classroom. These experiences are vital in helping shape well-rounded individuals and preparing them for future challenges and opportunities.”
A huge congratulations to every cast, crew and band member. Their dedication, talent and teamwork brought the production to life, making the school incredibly proud of their achievements.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prefects and Mentorship - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Prefects and Mentorship
We believe that leadership is about service, responsibility, and leading by example.
At the heart of our ethos is the spirit of service, and leadership opportunities are embedded throughout school life. Most of our students participate in the academic mentoring programme or act as a buddy to a new pupil, helping younger students adjust to new modes of study and school life.
In turn, our Sixth Formers develop strong interpersonal skills, deepen their subject knowledge, and gain valuable experience to support their UCAS applications.
For those who embody the school’s values and wish to serve in a more formal capacity, the Prefect system offers an opportunity to take on greater responsibility. Prefects are selected for their dedication, integrity, and leadership qualities, with each role having a distinct focus—whether assisting new students with their transition, organising charity events, or contributing to the smooth running of school life. Led by the Head Boy and his Deputies, the Prefect team upholds the values of St James, serving as role models and fostering a sense of unity and service within the community.
Through these experiences, students gain the confidence, communication skills, and sense of responsibility needed to make a meaningful impact both within the school and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pride and Achievement: St James Senior Boys’ School Marks Another Year of Fantastic GCSE Results  - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Pride and Achievement: St James Senior Boys’ School Marks Another Year of Fantastic GCSE Results
St James Senior Boys’ School is proud to announce another strong year of GCSE results, reflecting the hard work, commitment and resilience of our students.
This year, 34% of grades were awarded at 7–9 (A–A*), with 76% achieving 5–9 (C–A*). Several students achieved a clean sweep of top grades, including Rashid A-S, Rohan B-N, Peiyu N, Tej K, Oscar P, Zeyad S, Finn M, Noah S, Luke M and Montana Y, who all secured a majority of grades 8-9.
Head, Mr Rick Clarke, commented:
“We celebrate the achievements of a wonderful group of young men today who have received their GCSE results. I am hugely proud of their efforts, and I know how much work has gone into their exam preparation.”
The school is particularly proud of the breadth of success across both core and optional subjects, reflecting the strength of teaching and the boys’ determination to excel. This year’s results highlight notable achievements in several departments, with 67% of French grades at 7–9, 47% of Physics grades and 50% of Chemistry grades reaching the same top standard. Sanskrit was a particular standout, with 100% of grades awarded at 7–9.
Oscar P, who plans to study Economics, Maths and Biology at A-Level, shared his reflections:
“The teachers here really helped with bringing you on as a person and getting the results out of you that you deserve. The resources, the revision techniques, are all that you could want here.” He goes on to say, “The sport also collaborated with our academic education which really helped to give us the mental space to take a break, and I think that really helped with getting my grades, so I’m really happy.”
Many of our students will now continue their educational journey into the Sixth Form at St James, where they will pursue A Levels in preparation for university and beyond.
“Behind the grades and beyond the statistical analysis of how they have all done, are the individual stories of perseverance, resilience and determination. I know that all of these boys, whatever their achievements, have grown into young men who care and who want to make a difference, and we know that they will do great things in the Sixth Form and beyond. We congratulate them all and we wish them all the very best for the next step in their education.”
Today’s results are not only a celebration of academic success but also a reflection of the resilience, determination and community spirit that define life at St James.

pageCache.pageTitle: Excellent A Level Results for the Class of 2026!   - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Excellent A Level Results for the Class of 2026!
We are delighted to share this year’s A Level results, which reflect the determination, hard work, and ambition of the Class of 2026!
Results this year include:
• 25% A*-A • 47% A*-B
We are particularly proud to celebrate the individual successes of our students, including Oliver T (A*A*A), Christopher B (A*BB), William K (AAA), Thomas C (AAA), Devan G (AAA) and Daniel J (AAB).
A strong number of students have secured places at their first-choice universities, including the London School of Economics, Cardiff University, University of Edinburgh, Kings College London and University of Surrey, with many achieving impressive results in challenging subjects.
The school is pleased to see another increase this year in the number of students achieving A*–A grades. These results reflect not only the dedication and commitment of our students, but also the expertise and support of our staff. We are incredibly grateful to our teachers and wider school community for their hard work and the important role they have played in supporting our students.
At St James, we want our students to achieve their best while feeling supported throughout their time with us. We encourage them to challenge themselves, grow in confidence and take responsibility for their learning. With strong teaching, pastoral support and our distinctive quiet time practice, students develop the focus and resilience they need to succeed at school and in the future.
Congratulations to the Class of 2026. We are incredibly proud of each of you and the contribution you have made to our school community. We wish you every success as you take your next steps.

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebrating a Year of Outstanding GCSE Results - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Celebrating a Year of Outstanding GCSE Results
We are delighted to celebrate another successful year of GCSE results, with students achieving strong grades across a broad range of subjects.
This year, 47% of all grades were awarded at 7–9, equivalent to A–A*, up from 34% in 2025. Meanwhile, 91% of grades were awarded at 5–9, equivalent to C–A*, compared with 76% last year.
A number of students achieved particularly impressive results, with Karamveer B and Ayush O each achieving nine grade 9s and one grade 8, while Ryan F, Rohit K, Zakariya A, Owen B and Joshua M all secured a majority of grades at 8 or 9.
There were strong results across both core and optional subjects. Design & Technology was a particular highlight, with 74.29% of grades awarded at 7–9, followed by French at 62.5% and Physics at 52.7%. Mathematics also saw strong results, with 50.79% of grades awarded at 7–9.
Head, Mr Rick Clarke, said:
“I am so pleased with the wonderful GCSE results achieved by Year 11. We are proud of their efforts and delighted that so many of them achieved their target grades, with many of them doing even better than expected. Many of this year’s students will now continue into the Sixth Form at St James, where they will begin the next stage of their education and prepare for life beyond school. For those leaving St James, we wish them all the very best for the future and look forward to seeing all that they go on to achieve.”
While today is an opportunity to celebrate some excellent academic achievements, it is also a chance to recognise the hard work, determination and progress of every student. We are incredibly proud of all they have achieved. Well done Year 11!

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior Boys School Fees & Bursaries • St James School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Fees and Bursaries
We offer a balanced education where creativity, academic success and spiritual well-being walk hand-in-hand.
At St James Senior Boys’ school our mission is to provide a deeper learning experience, creating an environment where each pupil can thrive and reach his full potential. We believe in a brighter future for every boy, one where he can be his best self.
St James is committed to broadening access to the school by offering eligible parents or guardians bursaries to help with school fees. Bursaries are awarded on a means-tested basis and can cover up to 100% of fees, depending on need.
Schedule of Fees
Fees for the 2026/2027 academic year are as follows:
£9,990 (including VAT) per term
Lunches (vegetarian) are provided free within the basic fee.
Fees are payable in full by the first day of each term. All fees are to be paid by direct debit unless otherwise arranged with the Bursar.
Registration: There is an initial registration fee of £150 which is non-refundable.
Acceptance Deposit: There is a standard acceptance deposit of £2,000 (whole term’s fee for non-UK residents).
For monthly payment, the school has an arrangement with School Fees Plan. More information is available here.
Bursaries
All current parents, and parents who have completed their registration for admission are entitled to apply for a bursary. St James uses an external company to provide an independent review of individual circumstances. This review will include a home visit (or teams call if not able to facilitate a home visit).
Parents who wish to apply for help with fees must confirm to the school no later than the last Friday in the October prior to the academic year of entry.
Please note pupils applying via a pre-test are not able to apply for bursary funding.
If you would like further information about the process, please email the Bursary Secretary on bursary-applications@stjamesschools.co.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior Boys School Scholarships • St James School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Scholarships
Our Scholarships are available for Sport, Drama, Art and Music
Scholarships for Sport, Drama, Art and Music are awarded to pupils who show outstanding potential in their given area.
All candidates must demonstrate a strong commitment to, and enthusiasm for, their chosen scholarship subject. Only Year 7 and Year 9 applicants can submit an application. No scholarship application will be accepted unless the candidate is in receipt of an offer of a place.
We also offer Academic Scholarships, awarded to candidates who demonstrate an outstanding performance in the entrance assessments and interview.
Application Process for Sport, Drama, Art and Music for entry in September 2027.
Applications for scholarships September 2027 entry close on Friday 22 January 2027. A form and where requested supplementary evidence must be submitted by this date.
Please note that we can only accept one scholarship application per child.
All scholarships: Unfortunately, due to students needing to perform and be assessed alongside their peers during the scholarship process, candidates must attend on the date specified by the School. Alternative dates are not available.
If you have any questions about the process, please check the Scholarship Policy or contact our Registrar on 01784 266 933 or email admissions@stjamesboys.co.uk
Sports
Sports Scholarships are available for outstanding sportsmen or for those who display exceptional sporting potential. For external applicants Sports Scholarships are available at 11+ and 13+ entry. They must be aspiring to play at County and/or National Level in one of the school’s main sports (Basketball, Cricket, Rugby, Football, Hockey, Tennis and/or Athletics). For all applicants an ability to learn and a willingness to contribute fully to school sport across all three terms and a desire to further their sporting career are essential.
Those students who have already been offered an academic place at St James Senior Boys’ School and are interested in a Sports Scholarship, will be guided on how to complete an application.
This must be accompanied by a sporting reference from their main sport outside of school or their head of PE if they only play sport at school and sent to admissions@stjamesboys.co.uk by the specified deadline date.
Applicants will be expected to attend the school for a practical assessment day and an interview with the Director of Sport or one of the PE team on a date specified by the School.
Music
Music Scholarships are available for outstanding musicians or to those who show outstanding potential on an instrument. For external applicants Music Scholarships are available at 11+ and 13+ entry. They must be playing at a high level – involved in District and/or National orchestras and have achieved Grade 4 (or equivalent) or above at age 11. Applicants who can play an instrument in the St James orchestra will be favoured over those playing instruments that do not normally feature in a classical orchestra (e.g. Violin, viola, cello, flute, trumpet etc.)
Those students who have already been offered an academic place at St James Senior Boys’ School and are interested in a Music Scholarship, will be guided on how to complete an application.
If a reference is available outlining what ensembles etc. the boy has been a part of, this should be sent to admissions@stjamesboys.co.uk by the specified deadline date, but is not essential.
Applicants will be expected to attend an audition on a date specified by the School, which will consist of:
Auditions will be held by the Director of Music.
Sight reading
Aural tests, including singing
Interview with the Director of Music
Drama
Drama Scholarships are available for outstanding actors or to those who show outstanding potential as performers. For external applicants Drama Scholarships are available at 11+ and 13+ entry. Students should demonstrate a dedicated interest and exceptional potential ability as an actor on the stage.
Those students who have already been offered an academic place at St James Senior Boys’ School and are interested in a Drama Scholarship, will be guided on how to complete an application.
This must be accompanied by submission of a letter (1 Side of A4) detailing their performance history and reasons why their interest should be considered, through admissions@stjamesboys.co.uk mailbox by the specified deadline date.
Applicants will be expected to attend an audition on a date specified by the School, which will consist of:
Art and Design

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care & Safeguarding - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care & Safeguarding
At St James, we don’t just see pupils who are here to learn, we see people who are here to thrive.
Pastoral care is overseen by our Heads of Year and the Assistant Headmaster Pastoral, all of which are trained mental health first aiders. Supporting this system, we also have ELSA’s (emotional literacy support assistants) along with an in-school counsellor. This tiered approach provides tailored support for each individual pupil that may require it.
Each of our pupils are assigned to both a house and a form, wherever possible the pupil will have the same form tutor in Year 7 & 8 and through 9 –11. This helps to ensure that each pupil’s individual needs are known and therefore cared for.
We are also extremely fortunate that our timetable allows for each student to receive PSHE as a structured lesson each week. This ensures that important topics such as drugs and alcohol, grief and loss, sex and relationships are all covered with the depth and care that they deserve, and the student voice can play an important part of this subject. As part of the PSHE programme we of course invite specialist external speakers to talk on many of these topics.
As well as teacher support we also have a well-established peer buddying and mentoring programme.
In this, our new Year 7 pupils are buddied with both a Year 8 pupil and a member of our 6th form, allowing them to receive guidance from older pupils. This gives the younger students valuable insight as to how to thrive and adjust to new modes of study and schooling.
Safeguarding
At St James, we understand our vital role in protecting children from harm and fostering a secure environment where students can thrive. Safeguarding underpins every decision we make, with every member of our community dedicated to upholding the principles that support a strong safeguarding culture. Ensuring the safety and well-being of our pupils is not just a responsibility—it is a shared commitment to making a meaningful difference in their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Transport - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Transport
Our school is set in 32 acres of sprawling grounds in Ashford, Surrey.
We have a wide variety of transport options available to our families.
St James Ashford is easily accessible from across Surrey, South West London, Berkshire and the surrounding areas. The school is well connected by rail, public bus and our dedicated private school bus network.
Many of our pupils travel independently using public transport. Around 44% commute by train and a further 9% travel by public bus, demonstrating how convenient and well connected the school is. Ashford railway station is just a two-minute walk from the school, with regular services from London Waterloo, Reading and Windsor & Eton Riverside. For most pupils, journey times range from just 10 to 50 minutes.
Beyond practicality, what stands out most is our pupils’ enthusiasm for developing independence and resilience. Many enjoy their journeys, often highlighting the time spent with friends, making the school day an enriching experience from start to finish.
For families who prefer a dedicated school service, we operate a network of private school buses, providing safe and reliable transport from a number of surrounding areas. From September 2026, we’re expanding our school bus network with a brand-new A30 route, connecting families in Egham, Englefield Green, Virginia Water, Sunningdale and Ascot. Current private bus routes include: Kensington & Isleworth, Barnes & Richmond, Walton, Kingston, Ealing, and Old Windsor & Iver.
For further details on our private bus routes and to book, visit stjamesschools.vectare.co.uk.
For enquiries, please contact stjames@vectare.co.uk.
Please visit our Terms and Conditions for more information.

Academic Enrichment
At St James Senior Boys, we are very proud of how we stretch our strongest students. Those who demonstrate exceptional interest and ability in academic work, art, drama or notable sporting skills are given many opportunities to maximise their potential in each year group.
Each year our pupils enter school and national competitions such as the UK Maths Trust Challenge, Science Olympiads, Modern Foreign Languages Oxford University Writing Fiction competition or ISI Writing and speech competitions. We are an affiliated ‘Arkwright Scholarship School’, this programme is aimed at boys in set one in GCSE/A level Maths that also study a STEM subject. We have a wonderful Arts week competition which finishes with a Performing Arts Gala to celebrate and showcase our wonderful talent.
We celebrate academic success in our assemblies and have a Quality of Work Award notice board where the students’ work is recognised and rewarded for Academic excellence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Developing a true love of learning.
Our curriculum is carefully planned to ensure our pupils experience a broad range of subjects, developing a true love of learning and having the opportunity to find their true passions.
From the starting point in Year 7, they will typically go on to focus on nine or ten subjects at GCSE and three at A Level.
The Curriculum
Lower School Curriculum
In the Lower School at St James Senior Boys’ School we aim to provide students with a broad curriculum, helping them to explore different subjects and areas of interest. The aim is to inspire students and light a fire of interest in particular fields of study.
In these years most lessons are taught in Forms, allowing boys to forge relationships and work effectively in mixed ability groups. Mathematics and some Language classes are set by ability.
We want to ensure that the boys have the necessary skills that will equip them for success at GCSE and beyond, so have designed a Lower School Curriculum that places great emphasis on the development of key skills. We want to inspire the boys with a love of learning, to embrace a wider range of assessments such as oral presentation, in-depth project work, and traditional forms of written assessment. Through the Harmony Project and other cross-curricular initiatives, we look to make connections between learning and the world beyond the classroom.
Upper School Curriculum
At the end of Year 8, students choose their GCSE subjects from a broad range of options. Our academic aim is to enable a boy to develop his powers of reasoning and each subject provides a unique discipline as well as helping develop these skills in different ways.
Therefore, the balance of subjects is important. As part of a bespoke transition process entitled Stepping into Adulthood, the boys are provided with an extensive programme of support that equips them to make those important GCSE choices that will help shape their educational journey.
With a wide range of 22 academic subjects, the boys are offered a Renaissance education for the modern world. Whether it is studying ancient languages such as Latin or Sanskrit, the traditional Science, Arts and Humanities courses, or looking to the modern world of innovation in areas such as Design Technology, Media Studies or Computing, we offer a rich and varied curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: Life in the Sixth Form  - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
Life in the Sixth Form
A Sixth Form student has their own unique qualities, and we aim to nurture this through a combination of paedagogy, the familiar nature of a small community and school culture.
Small class sizes mean each student can be addressed as an individual, and a strong professional relationship between teacher and pupil is formed. Many of our pupils stay on with us so that they can continue to be part of this inclusive community, with familiar and driven staff and do so not just for their own academic success or personal development but to afford this chance to their younger peers through different leadership responsibilities.
Sixth Form students actively participate in the extra-curricular life of the school, from arranging Charity tea dances to refereeing sports fixtures for the younger teams as well as providing advanced mindfulness and philosophy classes to our Year 12 pupils to help them balance the academic with their personal and emotional growth. We have strong links with our sister school and have social events with them throughout the year.
Preparation for life beyond St James
Our students pursue a range of disciplines and career paths beyond St James. Support begins in Year 12 and each student receives advice pertaining to their journey after secondary education. Every student is advised on applications to university, apprenticeships and employment and all afforded the same opportunities. In the autumn term of Year 13, Sixth Form Tutors advise applicants on how to improve their personal statements, check their UCAS applications and collate the UCAS reference; interview practice and writing workshops as meets the student’s needs work in tandem with this and the strong bond between tutor and pupil means that they are supported throughout the process.

pageCache.pageTitle: St James Senior Boys’ School Named Finalist in Independent Schools of the Year 2025 Awards. - Independent Senior Boys School, Surrey
pageCache.text:
St James Senior Boys’ School Named Finalist in Independent Schools of the Year 2025 Awards.
St James Senior Boys’ School is delighted to have been nominated as a finalist for the School Trip of the Year in the Independent Schools of the Year 2025 Awards.
This recognition celebrates our distinctive approach to trips, which are carefully designed to enrich every stage of a student’s journey at St James. From local excursions to ambitious international expeditions, each experience is planned with purpose—encouraging self-discovery, resilience and reflection while strengthening the bonds of community.
Highlights of our programme include residential experiences during Activities Week, cultural and historical immersions in Europe, and challenging adventures such as our Alps Expedition and participation in the Nijmegen Marches. Whether students are climbing 4,000-metre peaks, walking 120km along the Camino de Santiago, or engaging with classical philosophy in Athens, they are constantly invited to step beyond the familiar and to grow in courage, curiosity and character.
Our trips are not just about travel; they are moments of transformation. Time and again, parents and staff remark on the visible impact these journeys have on our pupils—deepening their understanding of themselves, their peers, and the wider world. This award nomination is a testament to the vision, commitment and care invested by our staff, as well as to the enthusiasm and determination of our students.
We are proud that our programme has been recognised nationally and look forward to the awards ceremony later this year.
